key_insight: Parallel transversal controlled-Z gates could efficiently entangle neighboring trapped-ion registers while suppressing unwanted couplings.
engineering_relevance: For selected register sizes, geometric cancellation enables faster parallel operation than sequential two-qubit gates with a substantially lower required two-photon Rabi frequency.
method: Entangle corresponding ion pairs across neighboring wells in a double-well architecture.
Suppress unwanted couplings using tailored dynamical decoupling with pulse counts scaling quadratically in ion number.
Reduce pulse overhead through geometric cancellation.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes decoherence and laser-misalignment crosstalk, including their impact on fault-tolerant logical Bell-state preparation between two [[4,1,2]] code blocks.
watch_item: Performance depends on register size and control precision; the abstract reports feasibility analysis rather than an experimental demonstration.
paper_title: Parallel transversal entangling gates for fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computing
